title: The flock does not take the pastor's sense by blind obedience — but by the light of truth shown
source_text: XLIII. Veruntamen Scripturae sensum a Pastoribus suis commonstratum plebs fidelis non amplectitur caeca quadam obedientia, & propter eorum solam authoritatem, sed eo adducitur ipsa luce veritatis, quum ipsi semel indicata atque commonstrata est. Etenim difficilius est loci alicujus sensum invenire ac deprehendere, quam deprehensum ab alio & demonstratum, sola evidentia veritatis agnoscere & discernere. Quemadmodum multi sunt qui non possunt per se legere epistolam aliquam scriptam literis exolescentibus aut non satis apte formatis. Et tamen, postquam illis praelecta est, incipiunt agnoscere, & distinguere literarum ductus, & vident propriis oculis quid in illa contineatur.
pass_a_gloss: Nevertheless the faithful people does not embrace the sense of Scripture pointed out by its Pastors by a certain blind obedience, and on account of their authority alone, but is led there by the very light of truth, when once it has been indicated and pointed out to them. For it is more difficult to find and detect the sense of some place, than, detected by another and demonstrated, to acknowledge and discern it by the sole evidence of truth. Just as there are many who cannot by themselves read some letter written in fading letters or not sufficiently aptly formed. And yet, after it has been read aloud to them, they begin to acknowledge and distinguish the strokes of the letters, and see with their own eyes what is contained in it.
pass_b_english: Believers do not swallow a pastor's reading by blind obedience or bare office.
Once the sense is shown, the light of truth itself leads them to it.
Finding a sense is harder than recognizing it when another has demonstrated it.
Like faded handwriting: after it is read aloud, the eye begins to see the strokes for itself.
